## Summary Review of a caller of the reusable Daily Release (pm-ado#131, pinned to v2026.11.22) found a timing gap in the retirement guard of `daily-release.yml` and its continuation script. The workflow writes ONE publication journal entry before its retry loop, and the loop can call `npm publish` up to three times. The retirement guard reads that first entry. If the publish job stops after a late third call, a `retire-unpublished` dispatch can start its npm read more than ten minutes after the journal entry but less than ten minutes after the third publish call. An npm 404 in that interval lets retirement remove the active receipt. If the version then becomes visible on npm, hourly reconciliation no longer selects the retired candidate and cannot finish tagging it: a published version without tag or GitHub Release. A run that completes its post-loop reconciliation is not affected. ## Acceptance - A publication-attempt entry is recorded before EACH `npm publish` call; the first-attempt admission check stays as it is. - The retirement guard uses the newest attempt entry, and refuses retirement from an npm read taken less than ten minutes after it. A later read can still permit retirement when the other checks pass. - A test with three attempts, the last one late, proves that retirement is refused inside the window measured from the last attempt and allowed after it. - Callers get the fix through the pin bump; no caller change is needed. ## Related #314 (interrupted retirement cannot be completed by a retry) and #320 (interrupted candidate refresh): the same family of release-transaction gaps reported while reviewing caller migrations. --- ### GitHub comments (1) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-25T00:20:15Z) > > > > >
